children.translated_text: Wearing a silk garment resplendent with the luster of crushed yellow orpiment,
with lotus-feet soles beautiful with the radiance of a row of <s>javā</s> (hibiscus) flowers,
with body dark as the <s>tamāla</s> tree, face gracefully adorned with a gentle playful smile,

children.text: parānandābhogaḥ sphuratu hṛdi me ko.api puruṣaḥ ||1
children.translated_text: may that ineffable <s>Puruṣa</s>, the very fullness of supreme bliss, shine forth in my heart. ||1||
When He who is <s>Madana</s> (Cupid) to the hearts of the <s>gopīs</s> departed from the house of <s>Nanda</s>,
<s>Mukunda</s>, meeting the son of <s>Gāndinī</s> (<s>Akrūra</s>), [departed for] <s>Madhupurī</s> (Mathurā),
then she sank into the river of anxiety, with its dense, churning whirlpools,
in unfathomable waters of affliction—<s>Rādhā</s>, separated from her beloved. ||2||
Once, to dispel the fire of sorrow burning within,
she, with agitated mind, reached the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s> together with her friends;
from long familiarity with the arbors [of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s play], her mind
then clearly fell into a state of deep sleep—the dear friend [swooned]. ||3||
Then, with motionless limbs, [attended] with clusters of arranged lotus sprouts,
by those whose hearts feared a hundred misfortunes in the name of love,
whose tears from their eyes deepened the waves of the daughter of the Sun (<s>Yamunā</s>),
she lay dissolved upon the dust, encircled by her attendants. ||4||
Then, with her limbs resting upon the chest of <s>Lalitā</s>, fanned
with lotus petals cooled by the waters of the <s>Kālindī</s> (Yamunā),
as they perceived her throat trembling with the sprout of returning breath,
a sound full of great joy arose from the multitude of friends. ||5||
<s>Lalitā</s>, placing [<s>Rādhā</s>] upon the seat of lotus leaves,
then, setting foot on the path to fetch water, leaving <s>Rādhā</s>,
encountered on the sandy bank of the <s>Kālindī</s> one moving with playful gait—
she saw before her a certain sweet-voiced, white-winged one. ||6||
Then, upon seeing it, with heart slightly revived and with respect,

children.text: praṇāmaṃ śaṃsantī laghu laghu samāsādya savidham |
children.translated_text: offering obeisance, quickly approaching near,
seized with eagerness to carry a message to the court of <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: varaṃ dūtaṃ mene tamatilalitaṃ hanta lalitā ||7
children.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s> considered that most graceful one an excellent messenger—alas! ||7||
Setting aside, out of indignation, her jealous love toward the slayer of <s>Kaṃsa</s>,
she proceeded to tell the swan her heart's desire;

children.text: na tasyā doṣo.ayaṃ yadiha vihagaṃ prārthitavatī
children.translated_text: it is not her fault that she entreated a bird here,
for in whom does devotion born of love for <s>Hari</s> not place its trust? ||8||
You generally make your dwelling in pure waters,
you carry delight among lotuses, and you yourself are of pure nature;
therefore I, afflicted with sorrow and helpless, have taken refuge in you,

children.text: na yācñā satpakṣe vrajati hi kadācidviphalatām ||9
children.translated_text: for a request made to one of noble wings never goes in vain. ||9||
Having long forgotten us, who are distressed by the flames of the fire of separation,
the skilful enemy of <s>Madhu</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) dwells happily in the bustling [city of Mathurā];
therefore, placing this entire message in your own mind,
may you quickly reach the path to His abode. ||10||
May your path be free of obstacles and auspicious;
arise quickly, placing joy in your heart with due care;
running below with upturned eyes, swiftly,
may the curious, excited cowherd boys gaze upon you! ||11||
That ocean of cleverness—by the hard-hearted <s>Akrūra</s>,
by which [road] the lord of the lives of the cowherd women was swiftly taken away—
by that [road], the only one renowned in all the world, you must travel,
by that path, O ornament of the noble, indeed to the city of the <s>Dāśārhas</s> (Mathurā). ||12||
The doe-eyed <s>gopīs</s> with white cheeks flooded by streams of falling tears
are tormented there, overwhelmed by the force of love's passion;
you should recognize [that road] devoted to contact with <s>Hari</s>'s feet—
surely that is the chariot-wheel-marked path, O friend of love, the road of the chariot. ||13||
Drinking the sweet water of the daughter of the Sun (<s>Yamunā</s>), dark as the <s>jambū</s> fruit,
eating lotus stalks of soft luster like moonbeams,
pausing joyfully for a moment on a densely branched tree, O friend,
may you pleasantly set forth for the city of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> (Mathurā). ||14||
Crying out forcefully—[following the road by which] the beloved, met by the chariot-traveler <s>Akrūra</s>,
the host of cowherd women followed their beloved from afar;

children.text: tamādau panthānaṃ racaya caritārthā bhavatu te
children.translated_text: take that road first—may your journey be fruitful,
for this state of the supreme swan shines above all. ||15||
When <s>Hari</s> suddenly stole our garments,
which He climbed to stir up waves of hidden love—
concealing the sun's orb within its sprouts for you who are tireless,
that <s>kadamba</s> tree, O <s>kādamba</s> (swan), will quickly be your resting place. ||16||
Spreading beauty in every direction, with peacocks as her bards,
wearing an exceedingly pure garment of golden radiance,
with body dark as the <s>tamāla</s> tree, with face kissed by the gentle flute—
[that forest] where the manifest wave of supreme bliss sang wondrously. ||17||
By that [place] further, where the cowherd wives blossomed with the excitement of play—
their body-creepers [adorned] with dark musk-drops falling [from their brows]—
you should cultivate the joy of the <s>hallīsaka</s> dance that crushed the jasmine creepers,
all around in your mind, with that ground of the <s>rāsa</s> dance. ||18||
Beyond that, the hall of the spring-festival arts of <s>Manmatha</s> (Love) created by <s>Vāsantī</s>—

children.text: catuḥśālaṃ śaureḥ sphurati na dṛśau tatra vikireḥ |
children.translated_text: the courtyard of <s>Śauri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) glitters—do not scatter your glances there;
for if the joy born from seeing it causes you to forget your course of

children.text: kriye jāte tāvat tvayi bata hatā gopavanitā ||19
children.translated_text: action, then alas, the cowherd women are destroyed! ||19||
My purposes would be harmed by delay here; yet even if
you should behold all these places of <s>Hari</s>'s play,

children.text: taveyaṃ vyarthā bhavatu śucitā kaḥ sa hi sakhe
children.translated_text: let not your purity be in vain—for what, O friend, is that
virtue which would not serve to fix the mind upon the enemy of <s>Cāṇūra</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>)? ||20||
Where the cowherd women once gathered upon hearing the sound of the flute,
witness of secret play, beautified by bower-homes at every step—
that friend of the cows, the resting stone of the churner of <s>Madhu</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>),
<s>Govardhana</s> hill will instantly bring you joy. ||21||
That very mountain, fond of the embrace of the discus-marked hand,
we consider the crest-jewel among peaks on the face of the earth;

children.text: arātiṃ jñātīnāṃ nanu hariharaṃ yaḥ paribhavan
children.translated_text: for, surpassing <s>Hari</s> and <s>Hara</s>'s [mountains], the enemy of [<s>Indra</s>'s] kinsmen—

children.text: yathārthaṃ svaṃ nāma vyadhita govardhana iti ||22
children.translated_text: it truly made its own name meaningful: '<s>Govardhana</s>' (increaser of cows). ||22||
At the sight of the <s>tamāla</s> tree, in the vicinity of the hill, there are restless
<s>Pulinda</s> women, their bodies burning with the passion of remembering <s>Govinda</s>;

children.text: śanais tāsāṃ tāpaṃ kṣaṇam apanayan yāsyati bhavān
children.translated_text: gradually removing their burning pain for a moment, you shall go,
surely [cooling them] with breezes from your wings, chilled by the waters of the <s>Kālindī</s>. ||23||
Beyond that, a grove of <s>kadamba</s> trees, thrilling with the excitement of remembering <s>Śrīkānta</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>),
a garden of <s>kadambas</s> manifesting an array of aesthetic delights—

children.text: tvamāsīnastasyāṃ na yadi parito nandasi tato
children.translated_text: if, seated there, you do not fully rejoice all around, then
your fondness for dwelling amidst dense sweetness has been in vain. ||24||
Rivaling a row of autumn clouds, the dried head of the demon <s>Ariṣṭa</s>—
you will see it long dried in the precincts of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>;
from afar the servants of the friend of the Lord of <s>Kailāsa</s> (<s>Śiva</s>)
approach to climb it, confused in mind, [mistaking it for a peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>]. ||25||
Calling out, go freely; those whose beauty is kissed by the glow of twilight—
many beautiful women dwell in the land of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, O friend;
they will turn back, comparing [your cry to] the sound of <s>Murajiṭ</s>'s (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s) anklets,
their breath swiftly departing at the sound of your journey. ||26||
Seated comfortably on a branch where the fierce rays of the sun are filtered,
you should rest for a moment on the <s>bhāṇḍīra</s> fig tree of dense, dark beauty;
then, bearing the swan across the entire sky as a wondrous spectacle,
it will resemble the ever-growing <s>Viṣṇu</s> holding a faint discus. ||27||
You, [sprinkled] by eight eyes streaming with pure love's tears,
repeatedly bathing the pillar, O clever one, at the abode of the four-faced <s>Brahmā</s>—
you should depart from that famous [grove]; clearly, your kinsman's chariot
the goddesses of <s>Brahmā</s>'s forest will think has entered, when you arrive. ||28||
On the slippery path of surging waves of tears from their eyes,
with stumbling footsteps, their minds agitated by anxious delay—
when <s>Hari</s> plunged into that [lake], hastened by the <s>Yamunā</s>'s current,
the <s>gopīs</s>, cast about by longing, attained some indescribable state. ||29||
Where the pride of playful sport was repeatedly matched with the joy of dance,
with serpent-hood jewels fallen from their setting, smoke-hued—
before that [spot], fragrant with the pollen of <s>nīpa</s> tree blossoms,
you should drink the sweet, sacred water at the lake of <s>Kāliya</s>. ||30||
Of her whose body is scorched by the spring of separation from the enemy of <s>Tṛṇāvarta</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>),
who always knows the exaltation of being honored with love by the host of cowherd women—
you should perform for <s>Vṛndādevī</s>, whose sorrows are increased by the burden of fresh flower-clusters,
with supreme humility, the rite of salutation. ||31||
Thus, having crossed the eleventh forest resounding with the cries of peacocks,
enter this twelfth, <s>Madhuvana</s>, made dense with mango trees;
in which stands the city whose spotless fame of the birthplace of the <s>Yadu</s> clan—
surrounded the earth's expanse with streams of glory. ||32||
Filled with houses rivaling the young peaks of <s>Giriśa</s>'s (<s>Śiva</s>'s) mountain,
splendid with rows of supporting pillars, with flowering gardens,
situated on the banks of the <s>Kālindī</s>—it will shelter you, O friend—
<s>Madhupurī</s> (Mathurā), with its crowds of sweet waters, [will grant you] complete bliss. ||33||
In which <s>Śambhu</s>'s (<s>Śiva</s>'s) bull (<s>Nandī</s>) grazes on fresh fodder in one place—
of <s>Viriñci</s> (Brahmā), in another place a swan swallows the expanse,
somewhere a peacock, enemy of <s>Kroñca</s>, devours the serpent,
when licked by the <s>śallakī</s> (Boswellia) tree, the elephant of the enemy of <s>Vala</s> (Indra's elephant) takes it as a tender shoot. ||34

children.text: arodhiṣṭhāḥ kāyān na hi vicalitāṃ pracchadapaṭīṃ
children.translated_text: You did not restrain your body, nor did you notice the displaced covering garment
falling away on every path, nor even the pearl necklace loosened and dropped.
O you whose heart is intoxicated with the wine of remembrance of <s>Śrī Govinda</s>,
you are renowned as a 'faithful wife' — this clan of unchaste women laughs at that! ||35
Placing her left foot, with the lac-dye unwashed from it,

children.text: prayātāhaṃ mugdhe virama mama veśaiḥ kimadhunā |
children.translated_text: 'I have already gone out, O innocent one — stop! What use are these adornments to me now?'
From the intense commotion of the city women, O friend, I greatly suspect
that the flower-arrowed god of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> (Kṛṣṇa/Kāmadeva) triumphs before the balconies! ||36
He whose playful sidelong glances bathe the city streets and their surroundings,
wearing a fresh <s>aśoka</s> blossom as his crest-ornament, the conqueror of <s>Kaṃsa</s> moves forward.
Why do you alone, O fixed-eyed one, push us away from this jeweled palace rooftop,
and even block the row of latticed windows? ||37

children.text: muhuḥ śūnyāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ vahasi dhyāyasi sadā
children.translated_text: Again and again you cast an empty gaze, you constantly meditate,
though you plainly hear the hundreds of reports from your new attendants.
Therefore I suspect, O lotus-faced one, that the dark-complexioned radiance
of that youth has assumed embodied form as a traveler on the pathway of your eyes. ||38

children.text: vilajjaṃ mā rodīriha sakhi punaryāsyati hari-
children.translated_text: 'Do not weep shamelessly, O friend — <s>Hari</s> will come again
to take up the service of attending to the play of your sidelong glances.'

children.text: iti svairaṃ yasyāṃ pathi pathi murārerabhinava-
children.translated_text: Thus, on every path, when <s>Murāri</s> (Kṛṣṇa) made his fresh
entrance, the passionate love-talk of the women grew and multiplied. ||39
O friend, having directly beheld the moon-face of <s>Dāmodara</s>,
their minds kissed by waves of radiant love-bliss,
may the city women of <s>Mathurā</s> bestow delight upon your eyes,
they whose glory surpasses even the assembly of <s>Ābhīrī</s> (gopī) women! ||40
Then, wandering and wandering, through progressively narrower
dwellings of the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> clan, follow the city where <s>Madhava</s> resides,
where the enemy of <s>Mura</s>'s inner palace chamber triumphs,
with its banners obscuring the sky, tormenting the earth with splendor. ||41
On whose terraces tall crystalline pillars stand all around,
with steps fashioned from clusters of emeralds strung on coral,
swans, thinking them friends, born of the lotus (<s>Ambujabhū</s>, Brahmā),
with sweet calls, would at once respectfully perform service to them. ||42
That which was not found for ages by the clans of cowherd women
searching in the groves on the banks of the <s>Kālindī</s> (Yamunā),
O companion, his face always lit with a smile delighting the world,
shall I behold again the slayer of <s>Mura</s> shining forth before me? ||43
'Do not despair! This statement is true and made in haste —
he shall come, O <s>Rādhā</s>, your friend wearing a fresh peacock feather!'
Thus spoke a pair of parrots in the garden made by <s>Indra</s>'s younger brother (Kṛṣṇa),
which was overheard by the flocks of <s>Ābhīrī</s> women when <s>Uddhava</s> was at hand. ||44
Dark as a cloud, upon the terrace of <s>Hari</s>'s palace, a tendril of incense smoke
praised by the naive peacocks and fashioned without <s>aguru</s> (aloewood) rises,
O steadfast one, if from seeing that your mind's lustre sparkles like a swan,
then victory is won freely through the love of dwelling with water! ||45
Then, toward the middle chamber, with its new latticed windows and peacocks,
its swaying pearl-strands gleaming, its rows of spotless pillars,
you shall behold the pleasure-pavilion of the conqueror of <s>Mura</s>,
whose wall-surfaces shine with the story of the Tenth Canto painted in gold! ||46
On whose balcony stands a spotless staff made of emerald,
upon which at night a drowsy, intoxicated peacock with beautiful plumage roosts,
fearlessly climbing to its top, dispelling fatigue —
wait there, O brother, for the auspicious moment of the Lord of the <s>Yādavas</s>! ||47
Seated upon a couch made soft with the whitest cushions,
his body slightly arched at the pinnacle of the three worlds' splendors,
joyfully placing before him a pillow resembling the full moon,
upon which rests the burden of his two lotus-like hands, ||48
his complexion beautiful as the rising waters of the <s>Kālindī</s>, his appearance charming,
gazing within at the loveliness of jeweled <s>makara</s>-shaped earrings reflected in his cheeks,
wearing silk that surpasses the splendor and fragrance of gold,
<s>Mukunda</s> shall directly sprinkle your eyes with the nectar of delight! ||49
<s>Vikadru</s>, the most senior elder of all the <s>Yadu</s> lord's clans,
seated nearby, will always be singing sweet compositions,
and before him, that stern one named 'terror of the <s>Ābhīrī</s> women,'
leaning against a jeweled pillar, will be recounting tales of the <s>Kuru</s> dynasty. ||50
The crest-jewel of the <s>Śini</s> clan, accompanied by <s>Kṛtavarmā</s>, on both sides
will be carrying out the duty of waving a pair of fans,
and he, resting on his knees upon the jeweled floor, will be
a disciple of the guru, devoted to massaging his lotus feet! ||51
The king of birds (<s>Garuḍa</s>), with joined lotus-hands, on the ground before him,
seated and attentive, his mind fixed on every command,
at whose pair of wings the bards dwelling in <s>Mathurā</s>
would abandon their mutual quarrels born of competing <s>Sāma</s>-melody recitations. ||52
Even the clever four-faced one (<s>Brahmā</s>) is unable to describe
the beauty of the radiance of the toenail of the little toe of <s>Dāmodara</s>'s foot,
yet due to the easily acquired fickleness of a woman's wit, I
have embarked upon describing his form — such is the great audacity of love! ||53
His toenails, whose tips are polished by the crest-gems of
<s>Svayambhū</s> (Brahmā), bewildered by the theft of the cowherd boys of <s>Vraja</s>, shine resplendent,
beholding which for even a moment, overwhelmed by manifest supreme bliss,

children.text: sa devarṣirmuktān api tanubhṛtaḥ śocati bhṛśam ||54
children.translated_text: that divine sage (<s>Nārada</s>) deeply laments even for the liberated souls. ||54
An array of lotuses, aspiring to the beauty of his feet,
adopted the vow of forlorn exile, rich in passionate color,
I salute the frost, for though it pursues improper conduct,
it inflicts upon these lotuses the punishment of death year after year. ||55
The splendor of whose pair of thighs swallows the pride
of thick emerald-like plantain clusters with its radiant beauty,
upon whose pillar-like brilliance as a tethering post depends
the she-elephant of the cowherd women's hearts, wild with passion and unrestrained. ||56
O friend, in the matter of sustaining the <s>sapharī</s>-fish-like eyes of the <s>Ābhīrī</s> women,
the cause is his navel-lake, endowed with the expanse of depth,
from which, at the beginning of the <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic cycle), arose the lotus
bearing the worlds within, deep as the canopy from which the rain-cloud creator emerged. ||57
O friend, whose belly bears the radiance of the narrow triple-fold creases,
the belly that is skilled in the art of wearing away the binding ropes,
within whose belly <s>Yaśodā</s> once through the mouth-gate
beheld the three worlds, twice over, surrounded by gods, men, and serpents! ||58
Upon whose broad chest shines the encircling <s>vanamālā</s> (forest garland),
instantly arousing <s>Manasija</s> (Kāmadeva, the god of love) in the minds of slender women,
upon which the <s>Kaustubha</s> gem, sweet to the world, ever bears
a firefly-like glow, though equal in brilliance to the sun's own rays. ||59
Radiant with the splendor of pairs of emerald pillars blooming all around on the balustrade,
lovely with armlets pressed by <s>Keśi</s>-demon-slaying arms,
intent on embracing the golden throats of gopīs languid with passion,
his pair of arms, distinctly fragrant, triumphs! ||60
It claims sovereignty in the world — a fresh wave of beauty,
sweet with the inner ripening of joyful <s>Madana</s>'s (Kāmadeva's) rapture,
a playground of the nectar of a new smile with dancing eyebrow-vines,
with teeth resembling a row of gleaming pearls — such is his face! ||61
'What use are these elaborate descriptions? Let me state clearly,
O friend, this is without doubt merely a basis for recognition:
he in whom supreme bliss will be visible, shining upon the pathway of your eyes,
he is to be known by you, O sweet-voiced one — that is <s>Madhuripu</s> (the enemy of Madhu, Kṛṣṇa)!' ||62
Should you behold <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> bewildered and enchanted
by the arts of passionate play of intoxicated, graceful swan-like women and the charms of city brides,

children.text: tadā nāsmān grāmyāḥ pravaṇapadavīṃ tasya gamayeḥ
children.translated_text: then do not lead us rustic women onto the path of approach to him —

children.text: sudhāpūrṇaṃ cetaḥ kathamapi na takraṃ mṛgayate ||63
children.translated_text: a heart filled with nectar does not in any way seek buttermilk! ||63
When he restrains aloud the cooing of the cuckoos, which is the cause
of waves of remembrance of <s>Vṛndāraṇya</s> (Vṛndāvana) and its delights,
or when breezes blow carrying the fragrance of the mountain jasmine,
then and only then deliver our message to the slayer of <s>Mura</s>! ||64
Formerly dwelling among the cowherds, out of love for all the women,
you, O lover of the <s>gopīs</s>, bestowed upon one of them the weight of special honor,
her friend <s>Lalitā</s>, the spirited and graceful one, conveys this petition
bowing at the vicinity of the golden pedestal of your blessed lotus feet: ||65
'With great care, from childhood, with clusters of fresh lotus tendrils,
alas, you nurtured her growth again and again,
and after long, she became a full-bodied heifer with heavy udders and swelling hips —
O slayer of <s>Mura</s>, this is that same <s>Kapalikā</s> (the little cow/the skull-bearer)!' ||66
Near the <s>nīpa</s> (kadamba) trees, she who had only three or four leaves — alas — was led by you
to follow the ways of companionship with the beloved of the <s>mākanda</s> (mango-loving cuckoo),
This is that spring, O lover of the <s>gopīs</s>, which under the pretext of shedding pure streams of honey,
weeping before us, makes us weep. ||67

children.text: prasūto devakyā madhumathana yaḥ ko.api puruṣaḥ
children.translated_text: O slayer of <s>Madhu</s>, that certain person born of <s>Devakī</s>,
has gone to the abode of the supreme bliss of the cowherds' prosperity.

children.text: dhṛto yo gāndhinyā kaṭhinajaṭhare samprati tataḥ
children.translated_text: He who was held in the hard womb of <s>Gāndinī</s> — now therefore,
alas, alas, the story of <s>Gokula</s> has entirely set. ||68
The beautiful cowherd women are harassed by <s>Ariṣṭa</s> (ill omen), approaching calamity;
<s>Tṛṇāvarta</s> (the whirlwind) has seized the courtyards, creating fear.
These surroundings of the dwelling land of <s>Vraja</s> have become void,

children.text: vahante santāpaṃ murahara vidūraṃ tvayi gate ||69
children.translated_text: bearing grief, O slayer of <s>Mura</s>, now that you have gone far away. ||69
O <s>Hari</s>, you must not come to the cowshed now by any means,
for the rows of creepers in the land of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> have become poisonous.
O slayer of <s>Madhu</s>, the fragrance of flowers deposited by the wind,

children.text: bhajan sadyo mūrcchāṃ vahati nivaho gopasudṛśām ||70
children.translated_text: instantly brings fainting upon the assembly of beautiful cowherd women. ||70

children.text: kathaṃ saṅgo.asmābhiḥ saha samucitaḥ samprati hare-
children.translated_text: How is association with us fitting now, O <s>Hari</s>?
We are mere village women, while your feet are worshipped by princesses.
Gone is the time when, eager for union with the cowherd women,
you stood in the darkness among the trees of the household gardens. ||71

children.text: vayaṃ tyaktāḥ svāmin yadi tava kiṃ dūṣaṇamidaṃ
children.translated_text: O Lord, if we are abandoned by you, what fault is this of yours?
This nature of the dark ones is exceedingly hard to overcome.
Crows, though familiar with cuckoos from having shared the nest since birth,
are immediately abandoned by them once they acquire new wings. ||72

children.text: ayaṃ pūrvo raṅgaḥ kila paricito yasya tarasā
children.translated_text: This is indeed a former stage, well known; with zeal,
with relish one should narrate it — consider this drama.
O lord of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, I must first ask you this:
do you remember, O wretched one, the pair of syllables '<s>Rādhā</s>'? ||73
O householder of the bower-valley-cave dwelling, will the hard-to-control
ways of the cowherd women now be spoken of in your absence?
Even she who was most skilled among the <s>gopīs</s> at your lotus feet —
that <s>Rādhā</s> has come to the state of asking ordinary, common questions. ||74
O ornament of the assembly, if this cowshed has been forgotten by you,

children.text: na tūrṇaṃ dhūmorṇāpatirapi vidhatte yadi kṛpām |
children.translated_text: and if even the lord of <s>Dhūmorṇā</s> (<s>Yama</s>) does not quickly show mercy,
how will my friend pass the succession of days, with the fragrances
of the flower-groves of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> becoming but seats of sorrow? ||75
With waves rivaling the ease of the <s>Yamunā</s>, Death's sister,
she has created some river in the cowshed with the flood of tears from her eyes.
As if out of spite toward her, proud Death does not hear

children.text: murāre vijñaptiṃ niśamayati mānī na śamanaḥ ||76
children.translated_text: this petition full of prayer for her desired state, O <s>Murāri</s>. ||76

children.text: kṛtākṛṣṭikrīḍaṃ kimapi tava rūpaṃ mama sakhī
children.translated_text: Having once seen from afar your form that plays the game of irresistible attraction, my friend,
her mind abandoning the knowledge of what is harmful and beneficial,
this wretched one, entering impetuously into the fire of love,
like a moth, O slayer of <s>Mura</s>, has repeatedly burned herself. ||77

children.text: mayā vācyaḥ kiṃ vā tvamiha nijadoṣāt paramasau
children.translated_text: What more should I say to you here? By her own fault, that
foolish one, O garland of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> flowers, has gone to distress.
The fire of sorrow that burns for your sake — even today from her heart
the foolish one does not remove you even a particle. ||78

children.text: trivakrāho dhanyā hṛdayamiva te svaṃ puramasau
children.translated_text: Ah, <s>Trivakrā</s> (Kubjā) is fortunate! Having reached your city,
as if it were your heart, she freely sports and dwells there.
Surely, O innocent one, my friend was born from a loss of merit,
since even a moment's entry there was not easily obtained by her. ||79
Is she possessed by spirits? Was she bitten by the serpent <s>Akrūra</s>?
Has she lost her mind from epilepsy? Did she suddenly collapse?
Thus, her anxious elders all around made various conjectures
about her, O slayer of <s>Mura</s>, who lay motionless upon hearing the sound of bamboo flutes. ||80
This new wave of the ripening of ill-fortune now
freely grinds within the cave of my companion's heart,
since, O you who dwell in <s>Mathurā</s>, sweet to the eyes of the world,

children.text: ścirādārtā vārtāmapi tava yadeṣā na labhate ||81
children.translated_text: she, long anguished, does not receive even news of you. ||81
She bows to <s>siddhas</s> and ascetics, worships groups of magicians,
serves with great humility those who know medicines.
For the consecration of seeing you, she devotedly serves <s>Girisutā</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>) —

children.text: manīṣā hi vyagrā kimapi śubhahetuṃ na manute ||82
children.translated_text: for her anxious mind does not disregard any auspicious means. ||82
The protector of cattle, the loving son and enemy of serpents,
whose play increases love, who steals the radiance of dense dark clouds,
who ever delights in sport near the hill of <s>Nandīśvara</s> —

children.text: bhavantaṃ kaṃsāre bhajati bhavadāptyai mama sakhī ||83
children.translated_text: my friend worships you thus, O enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, for the sake of attaining you. ||83
Tormented, having drawn you with the juices of crushed <s>tamāla</s> sprouts,
depicting the destruction of <s>Madana</s>'s bow by the curve of your eyebrows,
and placing the creeper of her own arms around your neck in the picture,
she rolls on the ground, her body dense with spreading numbness. ||84
Sometimes, bewildered, from the excess of intense remembrance of you,
this foolish friend of mine considers herself to be you.
Thus, O <s>Murāri</s>, the affliction of <s>Rādhā</s>, whose mind is consumed by the fire of separation,

children.text: murāre duḥsādhyā kṣaṇamapi na bādhā viramati ||85
children.translated_text: being incurable, does not cease even for a moment. ||85
Though cast off by you on top of all her torments,
even now your beloved friend impetuously follows your ways.
Since she, O enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, considers you hard-hearted,
she who was foremost among virtuous women has become broken-hearted day after day. ||86
'He sports openly before all those lovers intoxicated with pride' —
hearing this, she certainly falls into the deepest trance.
'He always frequents the path of the <s>Yamunā</s>' — O enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>,
hearing this, she clearly prepares herself to consider even <s>Yama</s> (Death). ||87
O <s>Murāri</s>, O one whose radiance is like blue lotuses blooming in the waters of the <s>Kālindī</s>,
O <s>Mukunda</s>, O <s>Madana</s> of auspicious <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, O jewel among the gods,
O joy of <s>Vraja</s>, O beloved of <s>Nandīśvara</s>, O son of <s>Nanda</s>, O <s>Hari</s> —
thus constantly crying out, she stirs up grief among her attendants. ||88
Scorched on all sides by the flames of the forest fire of separation from you,
distressed by the piercing attacks of the five-arrowed hunter (<s>Kāma</s>),
this deer of my companion's life-breath, having become emaciated, will soon abandon this body-forest,
O <s>Hari</s>, forcibly, today or tomorrow. ||89
When the moon, whose radiance swells like an ocean of milk, sweet with its frosty crest,
assumes through the play of glances the form of the conqueror of Love, my friend,

children.text: hare dattasvāntā bhavati tadimāṃ kiṃ prabhavati
children.translated_text: O <s>Hari</s>, surrenders her heart to it. Then what power has <s>Smara</s> (Love) to slay her?

children.text: smaro hantuṃ kintu vyathayati bhavān eva kutukī ||90
children.translated_text: But it is you yourself, O mischievous one, who torments her. ||90
O jewel of the <s>Yadus</s>, we understand the feelings of the cowherd women;

children.text: na jānīmaḥ kasmāt tadapi tava māyā racayati |
children.translated_text: yet we do not understand why your <s>māyā</s> (illusion) still creates this.
Since the wind-disease has entirely afflicted her inner being
by its force, her collection of sorrows has only been doubled. ||91
His guru's student now serves as counselor to the <s>Yadus</s>;

children.text: sakhīyaṃ kālindī kila bhavati kālasya bhaginī |
children.translated_text: this friend, the <s>Kālindī</s>, is said to be the sister of <s>Kāla</s> (Death).
Who else would there be in the king's city, known to me,
who, O ornament of the <s>Yadus</s>, reporting her condition, might persuade you? ||92
Her limbs shattered, anguished by the rolling upon inner wounds,
enveloped by ever-increasing afflictions of eclipse after eclipse,
her fragrance destroyed, all playful curiosity with her companions ceased —
O Moon, please make happy the night-lotus that is <s>Rādhā</s>, even by the touch of your feet. ||93
O <s>Śauri</s>, my companion has somehow protected her life from calamities,
her mind dependent on the desire for the joy of union with you.
Now that the appointed day has passed, despairing of life,
she fearlessly casts her glances upon the mango buds. ||94
Abandoned by her attendants whose resolve to begin remedies has weakened,
who have given up on her recovery, she who clearly suffers the torment of Love —
not relinquishing her attachment, the lotus-eyed one —
only a mere fraction of hope for meeting you today preserves her life-breath. ||95
O you who delight in the play of the <s>rāsa</s> dance, toward my friend

children.text: purā baddhā yena praṇayalaharī hanta gahanā |
children.translated_text: a deep, ever-new wave of love was formerly bound — alas!

children.text: sa cen muktāpekṣastvamapi dhig imāṃ tulaśakalaṃ
children.translated_text: If he who bound it is now indifferent, then shame on this tiny nose-ornament
that rests upon her nose and still moves even now. ||96
O <s>Mukunda</s>, with wandering eyes, whatever hundred unforeseen things she does,

children.text: vidhatte tadvaktuṃ jagati manujaḥ kaḥ prabhavati |
children.translated_text: who among mortals in this world is able to describe that?
But when the auspicious one, with longing mind, sometimes laments,
that I shall tell you — O Lord, lend ear to this path of <s>Makara</s>-crested Love. ||97

children.text: abhūt ko.api premā mayi murariporyaḥ sakhi purā
children.translated_text: 'O friend, there was formerly some love of <s>Murāri</s> toward me
which would not consider even the highest expectation of merit as worth relying on in comparison.

children.text: tathedānīṃ hā dhik samajani taṭasthaḥ sphuṭamahaṃ
children.translated_text: Yet now, alas, I have clearly become an outsider;
I feel such shame that I am ashamed even to live for a moment more.' ||98

children.text: garīyān me premā tvayi paramiti snehalaghutā
children.translated_text: 'My love for you is the greatest' — this would show lightness of affection;
'I shall not live' — this would be a method of proclaiming love's weight;
'Why do you not come?' — this would be a display of the succession of memories.

children.text: harau sandeśāya priyasakhi na me vāgavasaraḥ ||99
children.translated_text: O dear friend, I have no opportunity for words as a message to <s>Hari</s>. ||99

children.text: amī kuñjaḥ pūrvaṃ na mama dadhire kāmapi mudaṃ
children.translated_text: These groves did not formerly give me any particular joy;

children.text: drumālīyaṃ cetaḥ sakhi na katiśo nanditavatī |
children.translated_text: this row of trees, O friend, has not delighted my heart many times;
Now behold, these [signs] simultaneously bring about distress,

children.text: prabho muktopekṣe bhajati na hi ko vā vimukhatām ||100
children.translated_text: O lord, when you have become indifferent, who indeed does not turn away? ||100||
When, from the arising of eyes intoxicated by the awakening god of love,
forcibly attracting with the sweet melody of his flute,
I, whose vow as a chaste wife was repeatedly shattered by his playfully darting glances—
shall I behold the slayer of <s>Mura</s>, whose sidelong glances overflow with the intoxication of divine play? ||101||
O auspicious one, the time passed when the enhanced fragrance of amorous play—
desiring sport, in a mountain cave, with body concealed—

children.text: sa māṃ dhṛtvā dhūrtaḥ kṛtakapaṭaroṣāṃ sakhi haṭhā-
children.translated_text: that rogue, seizing me who feigned anger, O friend, forcibly—
drew me, pulling to his chest, [me] adorned with hundreds of crescent nail-marks ||102||
In the sweet onset of autumn, dear to the humming rows of bees,
at the forest's edge, whitened by waves of moonbeams,
when shall I, bold in the disputes of love-battle stirred by the god of love,
make <s>Govinda</s> a devoted lover through tight embrace? ||103||

children.text: mano me hā kaṣṭaṃ jvalati kimahaṃ hanta karavai
children.translated_text: Alas, my mind burns with anguish—what shall I do?

children.text: na pāraṃ nāvāraṃ kimapi kalayāmy asya jaladheḥ |
children.translated_text: I find neither the far shore nor a dam for this ocean [of grief];

children.text: iyaṃ vande mūrdhnā sapadi tamupāyaṃ kathaya māṃ
children.translated_text: I bow my head to you—quickly tell me a remedy,
for even a moment's particle of fortitude [cannot sustain me] from falling ||104||
If that hard-hearted crest-jewel [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] has departed, leaving me,

children.text: paryātu svacchandaṃ mama samayadharmaḥ kila gatiḥ |
children.translated_text: let him wander freely—my duty to our vow is indeed my refuge;

children.text: idaṃ soḍhuṃ kā vā prabhavati yataḥ svapnakapaṭā-
children.translated_text: who can endure this? For through the deception of dreams—
he comes here to <s>Vṛndāvana</s> and delights me with his arts ||105||

children.text: anaucityaṃ tasya vyathayati mano hanta mathurāṃ
children.translated_text: Alas, his impropriety pains my mind—to <s>Mathurā</s>
go and freely restrain that fickle-hearted <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: sakhi svapnārambhe punarapi yathā vibhrama madā-
children.translated_text: O friend, so that at the onset of dreams, intoxicated by passion's confusion, again—

children.text: dihāyāto dhūrtaḥ kṣapayati na me kiṅkiniguṇam ||106
children.translated_text: that rogue, coming here, does not undo the strings of my girdle-bells ||106||

children.text: ayi svapno dūre viramatu samakṣaṃ śṛṇu haṭhā-
children.translated_text: Oh, let the dream be far away! Listen—before your very eyes, forcibly—
do not be distrustful, O friend, thinking it mere mental delusion;
your dear friend [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], having reached the <s>Govardhana</s> forest, out of curiosity—
unexpectedly again displayed his expertise in the battle of love ||107||
Running in indignation through the dense thicket on a narrow path,
with the tinkling of my anklet-bells doubled by startled footsteps,
that playful one, his eyes brimming with joy, wishing to seize me—
did not notice the flute fallen from his lotus-hand to the ground ||108||
Unable to proceed because my new garment was caught
by creepers dappled with flower-smiles, as I wept,
that one who delights in jesting, O dear friend, seeing me with downcast face—
your friend approached for a kiss, his quivering lips like <s>bimba</s> fruit ||109||
Then I, O friend, having hidden the flute in my hair, slowly—
with feigned anger, with frequently moving eyebrows and a frown,
skilled in the playful art of hair-pulling and thieving conduct—
<s>Hari</s>, having found a pretext, forcibly led me to a mountain cave ||110||
Once, in the bower of <s>vāsantī</s> creepers, that bold one, impetuously,

children.text: hasan pṛṣṭhālambī sthagayati karābhyāṃ mama dṛśau |
children.translated_text: laughing, approaching from behind, covers my eyes with his hands;
wishing to discover [his identity], jealousy arising in me, O friend, I felt the tips of his fingers—

children.text: na jāne kutrāyaṃ vrajati kitavānāṃ kila guruḥ ||111
children.translated_text: I do not know where this master of deceivers goes ||111||

children.text: atīteyaṃ vārtā viramatu puraḥ paśya sarale
children.translated_text: Let this talk of the past cease—look ahead, O innocent one;
there is your dear friend, his face brightened by the sweetness of his smile,
with the splendor of his pillar-like arms, eager for the desired embrace—
that ocean of love-play throws a <s>bandhūka</s> flower at me ||112||
Therefore arise, O modest one, with the dense pearl necklace

children.text: vadhānemaṃ dhūrtaṃ sakhi madhupurīṃ yāti na yathā |
children.translated_text: let us bind this rogue, O friend, so that he may not go to <s>Madhupurī</s>,
thus, becoming numb from the experiences awakened by love,
she evokes the lamentation of her friends time and again ||113||
Alas, what suffering! In my wicked-heartedness, from youth, to my friend
who is naturally innocent, I repeatedly taught the knot of jealous anger;
from that beginning, O master of the <s>gopī</s> host's love, completely—
she did not attain, though eager, the force of your pure pillar-like arms ||114||
On the veranda fragrant with <s>Kālindī</s>'s lotuses, in the bower dwelling,
residing, with hair exuding the fresh fragrance of <s>vāsantī</s> flowers,
in your lap, with eyes gently closed in the bliss of sleep—this one again,
when shall I serve her, fanning with a cluster of tender sprouts? ||115||
Filled with bliss in the environs of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, by the autumn night's
exuberant play, with flowers loosened from her wilting braid,
with vine-like arms placed upon your shoulders, I—

children.text: kadā kuñje līnā rahasi vihasiṣyāmi sumukhīm ||116
children.translated_text: when, hidden in the bower, shall I secretly laugh at that beautiful-faced one? ||116||
'I am going far away to gather flowers; you meanwhile,
near the bank, arrange this <s>tulasī</s> spray'—
thus, with this pretext, knowing your presence, I—
when, O lover of the <s>gopīs</s>, shall I send her to the bower at the right moment? ||117||
Thus, the tale of <s>Gokula</s> at the lotus feet of the glorious enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>,
having reported to each, cultivate affection among his attendants;
O companion of the <s>kādambī</s> bird, bearing on your lap as an ornament
those whom the blessed Lord, overflowing with love, most graciously favored ||118||
O lover of the <s>haṃsī</s> (goose), first, to the <s>vanamālā</s> (forest garland) with its converging curves,

children.text: mudā kṣemaṃ pṛcchann idamupaharethā mama vacaḥ |
children.translated_text: joyfully inquiring about her welfare, offer this my message:
'Long dwelling upon the chest of the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, dear to his companionship—
O virtuous one, have you forgotten this doe-eyed one?' ||119||

children.text: idaṃ kiṃ vā hanta smarasi rasike khaṇḍanaruṣā
children.translated_text: 'Or perhaps—alas!—do you remember, O connoisseur, when in the fury of a lovers' quarrel,
my friend, with trembling limbs, at the slope of <s>Govardhana</s> hill,

children.text: bhiyā sambhrāntākṣaṃ yadiha vicakarṣa tvayi balā-
children.translated_text: in fear, with bewildered eyes, forcibly dragged toward herself,
seizing the lord of <s>Gokula</s>, whose fresh peacock feather was slipping?' ||120||
Then speak to the <s>makara</s>-shaped earring, with joy—
'Why this hesitation in inquiring about your welfare?'

children.text: rucismerā yā tvaṃ racayasi sadā cumbanakalām
children.translated_text: 'You, who with a radiant smile always practice the art of kissing,
touched by the sidelong glance reflected in the mirror-like cheek of the enemy of <s>Mura</s>, O friend' ||121||
'O goddess, with the thought that your abode is upon the ear-creeper,
I earnestly take refuge in you alone, with a loving heart;
secretly, away from the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, very softly, in the hollow of his ear,
O friend, tell <s>Hari</s> of <s>Rādhā</s>'s anguish, mingled with plaintive appeals' ||122||
To the <s>Kaustubha</s> gem, with love and humility, [convey] my embrace;
O best of birds, speaking thus, make this petition:
'O friend, has your forgetfulness of <s>Rādhā</s> also become unfathomable?

children.text: kathaṃ vā kalyāṇaṃ vahati tarale hi praṇayitā ||123
children.translated_text: How can an inconstant lover bear auspiciousness?' ||123||
With the constantly sounding jeweled girdle, bangles, anklets, and flute—
accompanied by the songs of wandering young women, O jewel of the gods,
will that scene truly come to be again, with <s>Hari</s>'s <s>tāṇḍava</s> dance—
an abundant festival of music, dance, and song on the banks of the <s>Kālindī</s>? ||124||
O conch, you are new; you have no acquaintance with the cowherd women,

children.text: na dhatse rādhāyāḥ guṇagarimagandho.api na kṛtī |
children.translated_text: nor have you acquired even the fragrance of <s>Rādhā</s>'s glorious qualities;
yet I beseech you, to fulfill the longing placed in my heart—
for those of pure nature bear love even when weary ||125||
O friend, joy of the ocean's heart, taking <s>Govinda</s>,
may you rejoice happily in the environs of holy <s>Vṛndāvana</s>;

children.text: kathaṃ vā te goṣṭhaṃ bhavatu dayitaṃ hanta balavān
children.translated_text: how indeed can the cowshed become dear to you? Alas—
for in this place the glory of the flute's everlasting fortune prevails ||126||
Thus, having placated each one overflowing with love's outpourings, in due order,
his attendants—O brother, listen—concerning the crusher of <s>Cāṇūra</s>,
again, broken by anger yet restless with love, near him,
narrate the tale adorned by his ten incarnations ||127||
To catch you, she cast the fish-hook of her mind baited with love—

children.text: mahāmīna kṣipraṃ nādhita rasapūre mama sakhī |
children.translated_text: O great fish, swiftly my friend was thus snared in the flood of passion;
having cut the string called discrimination, then you swallowed her—

children.text: hatāśeyaṃ kiṃ vā śiva śiva vidhātuṃ prabhavati ||128
children.translated_text: alas, alas! What can this despairing one do? ||128||
The poor girl, seeing the weight of charm of his beautiful form,
approached your vicinity, her mind elated with supreme curiosity;

children.text: tirodhāya svāṅgaṃ prakaṭayasi yat tvaṃ kaṭhinatāṃ
children.translated_text: that you, concealing your own form, display such hardness—

children.text: tadetat kiṃ na syāt tava kamaṭhamūrteḥ samucitam ||129
children.translated_text: is this not fitting for your tortoise (<s>Kūrma</s>) form? ||129||
O enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, even now there always shines, long-lasting, upon your
boar-formed (<s>Varāha</s>) body, clearly, a dense wave of love,
because that <s>Sairandhrī</s> (Kubjā), fond of sandalwood paste,
was embraced by you with utmost passion as your beloved ||130||
Long hidden within, the man-lion (<s>Narasiṃha</s>) form—from all sides,

children.text: stadīyo vyāpārastava tu na yayau vismṛtipatham |
children.translated_text: that activity of yours has not gone to the path of forgetfulness;
you, with gentle <s>Prahlāda</s>, O one of supremely cruel conduct—
are again engaged in tearing apart the hearts of others ||131||
When, in pride, disregarding elders, O <s>Vāmana</s>, with joy,
rich with castles in the air, she imagined herself turned toward you—
my dear friend has obtained this very fitting fruit of that:
that she is cast far away, fettered in the noose of love ||132||
This cruel one, O Lord, desires to fall like <s>Bhṛgu</s>, therefore—
That your hardness toward her is befitting, O <s>Bhṛgupati</s> (lord of the Bhṛgu lineage)!
This deed of yours is incomprehensible here — leading to the path of forgetting you,
since even that lord of <s>Nandīśvara</s>, who is directly the guru, was born [from you]. ||133||
The cows are joyless, long beset by the hordes of <s>Dūṣaṇa</s> (corruptors),
the slopes of <s>Govardhana</s> have suddenly become harsh like <s>Khara</s>, O ornament of the <s>Raghu</s> dynasty!
The cowherd settlement (<s>ghoṣa</s>) proceeds toward a state of <s>Virādha</s> (hostility) due to your sojourning abroad —
now <s>Mārīca</s> (illusion) clearly afflicts the women all around. ||134||
This time is propitious for rising again with <s>rāsa</s>-dance festivities,
O playful one, even now we are clearly without offense;
spreading upon your body a beauty rivaling the autumn sky,

children.text: kṛto na tvaṃ sīradhvaja bhajasi vṛndāvanamidam ||135
children.translated_text: O <s>Sīradhvaja</s> (plough-bannered one), being entreated, why do you not visit this <s>Vṛndāvana</s>? ||135||

children.text: na rāgaṃ sarvajña kvacidapi vidhatte ratipatiṃ
children.translated_text: O omniscient one, [she] creates no attachment anywhere, constantly hates <s>Ratipati</s> (the god of love),
commits treachery against the ordinances enjoined by the powerful,
long absorbed in meditation, always dwelling in <s>Saugata</s> (Buddhist) delight —

children.text: stathāpyasyāṃ haṃho sadayahṛdaya tvaṃ na dayase ||136
children.translated_text: yet, alas, O compassionate-hearted one, you show no compassion toward her! ||136||
With a sweet swarm of intoxicated bees, [driving away] the <s>mlecchas</s> (barbarians) of affliction,
with the sword-vine of love-buds that cuts and severs,
O <s>Kalki</s>, you who are seated here, delighting in the company of clever cowherd women,
may you restore this place, surpassing [all] in joyful heroism! ||137||
Thus, having conveyed the entire message whose verbal expressions are enclosed in the casket of love's outpouring,
with your face and surroundings moistened by tears from your eyes,
then, [drinking in] the reply of <s>Govinda</s>, like the nectar of honey,
seated, you should attend with your eyes for a moment, O lord of birds! ||138||
The son of <s>Nanda</s> must be brought into the path of direct experience,
service should be rendered to the <s>gopīs</s> who are honored throughout the world,
this <s>Mathurā</s> too, O clever one, can be reached in three or four <s>yāmas</s> (watches) —
so do not harbor this dilemma within, O lord of the flock of graceful she-swans! ||139||
Within whom shines with joy an unprecedented, pure radiance —

children.text: rvivektuṃ śakyete sapadi milite yena payasī |
children.translated_text: by whom, when two waters meet, they can immediately be distinguished —

children.text: kathaṃ kāraṃ yukto bhavatu bhavatastasya kṛtinā
children.translated_text: how can delay be fitting for that accomplished one like you
in the matter of meeting <s>Mathurā</s>, O lover of <s>Kādambinī</s> (cloud-maiden)? ||140||
Surrendered to love, always partaking of the <s>Bhāgavata</s>, he prevails,
turned away from the taste of worldly existence since birth, sweet with <s>bhakti</s> (devotion),

children.text: ciraṃ ko.api śrīmān jayati viditaḥ śākaratayā
children.translated_text: for a long time, a certain illustrious one triumphs, known for his austerity,
foremost among the steadfast, O ruler of the earth, like <s>Vaiyāsaki</s> (Śukadeva, son of Vyāsa)! ||141||
By connoisseurs (<s>sahṛdayas</s>), who are the repositories of <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic sentiments), its faults remain unnoticed,
honored for its form portraying the dense play of <s>Murāri</s> (Kṛṣṇa, the enemy of Mura),
may this composition, of that friend of all the worlds, that delightful one,
cause to blossom within the Lord a dense wave of joy! ||142||
